README: Single source of truth for card image constants: the size ladder, the
full-resolution dimensions, and the grid clause tables.
ladder: widths (px) the CDN serves for every card face; also the S3 key names
(str(width) + '.webp'). grid_src_default is the plain src= fallback width.
full: dimensions of the largest webp (matches Scryfall's source PNGs) -
the modal/card-page width/height attrs and the CSS aspect-ratio derive from it.
The sizes string is one clause per (density tier x layout breakpoint), and the
browser uses the first matching clause, so density tiers are ordered densest
first and each list ends with a null-condition default.
layout: [media condition, slot-width formula]. Formulas are the CSS grid slot
widths (body padding 1em x2, card padding 0.8em x2, gap 15px); each max-width
is one below the corresponding grid min-width threshold in styles.css.
density: [media condition, multiplier]. One tier: DPR >= 1.9 declares the slot
at 2/3, everything else unchanged. The guarantee is on UPSCALE (device px
painted / image px supplied), NOT on effective DPR. The browser picks
chosen >= slot * mult * DPR, so upscale = slot * DPR / chosen <= 1 / mult =
1.5x -- exact, device-independent, and attained. 1.5x is the industry-shipped
ceiling: it is what a '2x DPR cap' means on a 3x screen (Twitter's app and
YNAP's product grids both ship that cap, YNAP measuring -45% image weight on
an iPhone 11 Pro), and it is the top of Android's own 3:4:6:8:12:16 density
bucket ratios. Note it is a pure upscale bound, not literally a per-DPR cap:
on a 2x screen it permits effective DPR 1.333, which is stricter than an
as-written 2x cap would be. Two things are NOT invariants: the number of
ladder rungs a device drops (0 to 2), and effective DPR (chosen / slot), which
is lowest exactly where upscaling is gentlest and so reads backwards. One
pre-existing exception to the bound: where slot * mult * DPR exceeds 745 the
ladder tops out and upscale is whatever the ceiling gives, unchanged by the
budget -- that is why 1-column DPR-3 phones stay on the 745 at 1.35x, and a
DPR-4 phone ships 1.75x today. Most affected devices move from downsampling
(<1x) to a mild upscale. Grid cells don't earn full retina fidelity; the modal
always uses the full-width source (plain src, no srcset), 1:1 on desktop but
~2.0-2.4 effective DPR on phones, where .modal-image is capped at
min(450px, 85vw). Multipliers are strings so Python and JS emit byte-identical
text. Added rungs should keep the ladder geometric (uniform relative
quantization error); a finer ladder seats devices closer to the ceiling and so
reclaims overshoot without moving the ceiling.
See docs/issues/local-homepage-lcp.md for the design.
Consumers: api/noscript_helpers.py and scripts/copy_images_to_s3.py load this
file; api/static/app.js embeds a mirrored copy (app.test.js asserts it matches
this file, and the shared card-HTML parity fixture keeps both renderers'
output identical); card.js and styles.css can't read JSON, so app.test.js and
api/tests/test_noscript_parity.py assert their literals against this file.
